050-choose-concept-llm.did: Wrote the concept document that sets the visual strategy for the whole video. The argument is that an AI influencer only becomes sponsorable when the same face survives every post, so the real work is locking one character model rather than generating more images. The frame is casting versus contracting — most people re-cast their influencer on every generate, you audition once and sign that face to a contract. The recurring object is a single character card holding the anchor portrait, which starts as an empty frame with faces flickering through it, gets sealed when the model trains, is stamped out into every scenario, and ends up as the asset a brand is actually buying.
050-choose-concept-llm.issues: Two of the five register spans are both light and sit next to each other, separated only by a demo stretch. That is deliberate rather than padding — the video has one genuine problem-to-solution turn plus a short tension pocket where he says you need a content bank before approaching anyone, so there are three real dark-to-light flips in twenty minutes, not a flip every minute. The intro span is covered by a register even though the intro film now owns that stretch and will not carry cards.
050-choose-concept-llm.output: concept.json — thesis, frame, the-character-card through-line, and 5 register spans covering 99.3% of narration time (704.6s of 709.6s), lint green

130-author-intro-screenplay-llm.did: Authored and delivered the intro as ONE bespoke film (the new intro flow), then fixed an owner-reported overlap and hardened against its whole class. The film: 12 beats over the measured 90.7s intro, every clause verbatim, one character card born in beat 1 and carried as the SAME element to the last frame. Presenter is one girl-1 Avatar III clip, free at credits +0 seconds +0.
130-author-intro-screenplay-llm.issues: Owner spotted beat 4's rail and three dashed sponsor slots showing through the fourth card of beat 5's row for twelve seconds. Root cause was two beats claiming the same pixels while measuring in different frames of reference — beat 4 placed its mark column at x1420-1572 relative to the card at x820-1300 with the right third free, and beat 5 spread its row across the full canvas with slot four at x1380-1680. Space could not fix it: the row covers 81% of the canvas, so no band is free in both beats. The devices now LEAVE at 27.48s with autoAlpha rather than dimming to 30% — a dimmed stroke reads clean through a card whose fill is 8.5% white. Nothing mechanical had caught it because text_occluded is text-only, which is exactly the unenforced half of TASTE T7. Added a device-overlap audit to the composition that compares visible device bounding boxes at each beat midpoint; on its first run it confirmed the fix AND found a second defect nobody had seen, the beat-11 score column using a 76px pitch on 78px-tall rows. Recorded the lesson as TASTE-INTRO T11. Earlier in the same step: 7 lint errors were masking 19 layout errors, GSAP fromTo's immediateRender default parked the card half off-frame for the opening, and the gate caught 5.7s of frozen picture that every still frame passed.
130-author-intro-screenplay-llm.output: intro-film/out/intro.mp4 — 90.700s, 1920x1080, h264+aac, film gate pass, zero frozen stretches, zero device overlaps. Plus screenplay.json (12 beats, lint clean, mutation-tested), film/index.html with a declared LAYOUT grid and the overlap audit, and TASTE-INTRO.md T11.
